sources.entry: Gogs - Painless self-hosted Git Service written in Go. (Source Code) MIT Go

summary.one_liner: Gogs is a painless, self-hosted Git service written in Go, distributed as a single independent binary for platforms Go supports.
summary.what_it_does: Gogs provides a self-hosted Git service with a web interface covering user, organization and repository management. It supports access to repositories over SSH, HTTP and HTTPS, plus issues, pull requests, wiki, protected branches and collaboration tools. Repositories can be migrated or mirrored from other code hosts, and webhooks can notify Slack, Discord and Dingtalk. Authentication options listed include SMTP, LDAP, reverse proxy, GitHub.com and GitHub Enterprise, with 2FA. The README lists PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite3 as database backends.
use_cases: Host private Git repositories for a small team
Mirror or migrate repositories from other code hosts
Manage repository issues and pull requests on your own server
Deploy a lightweight Git server on a Raspberry Pi or small VPS
how_to_run: Follow the installation guide in the official Gogs documentation
notable: Distributed as an independent binary across platforms Go supports, including Linux, macOS, Windows and ARM
Designed to run on very modest hardware, such as a Raspberry Pi or 64MB RAM container
Supports webhooks to Slack, Discord and Dingtalk
caveats: README recommends at least 2 CPU cores and 512MB RAM for teamwork
Smallest officially supported browser resolution is 1024x768
API support is described as experimental
